[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.22] (4) The court may receive evidence that would not, but for this rule, be admissible in a court of law. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.22] (5) Every party shall be entitled to adduce evidence and to cross-examine witnesses during any hearing or part of a hearing from which that party and that party’s legal representative are not excluded. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.22] (6) A special advocate shall be entitled to adduce evidence and to cross-examine witnesses. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.22] (7) The court may require a witness to give evidence on oath. ## Filing and service of relevant material

## 80.23

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.23] (1) The Secretary of State is required to make a reasonable search for relevant material and to file and serve that material in accordance with the rules in this Part. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.23] (2) The duty to search for, file and serve material under paragraph (1) continues until the proceedings in question have been determined. ## Closed material

## 80.24

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.24] (1) The Secretary of State –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.24] (a) must apply to the court for permission to withhold closed material from a relevant party or the relevant party’s legal representative in accordance with this rule; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.24] (b) may not rely on closed material at a hearing on notice unless a special advocate has been appointed to represent the interests of the relevant party. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.24] (2) The Secretary of State must file with the court and, at such time as the court directs, serve on the special advocate –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.24] (a) the closed material;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.24] (b) a statement of the Secretary of State’s reasons for withholding that material from the relevant party; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.24] (c) if the Secretary of State considers it possible to provide a summary of that material without disclosing information contrary to the public interest, a summary of that material in a form which can be served on the relevant party. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.24] (3) The Secretary of State may at any time amend or supplement material filed under this rule, but only with–

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.24] (a) the agreement of the special advocate; or

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.24] (b) the permission of the court. ## Consideration of the Secretary of State’s objection or application

## 80.25

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (1) This rule applies where the Secretary of State has –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (a) objected under rule 80.21(5)(b) to a proposed communication by the special advocate or to the form in which it is proposed to be made; or

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (b) applied under rule 80.24 for permission to withhold closed material. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (2) The court must fix a hearing for the Secretary of State and the special advocate to make oral representations, unless –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (a) the special advocate gives notice to the court that he or she does not challenge the objection or application;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (b) the court has previously considered –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (i) an objection under rule 80.21(5)(b) to the same or substantially the same communication; or

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (ii) an application under rule 80.24(1) for permission to withhold the same or substantially the same material, and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] is satisfied that it would be just to uphold that objection or to give permission without a hearing; or

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (c) the Secretary of State and the special advocate consent to the court deciding the issue without a hearing. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (3) If the special advocate does not challenge the objection or the application, he or she must give notice of that fact to the court and the Secretary of State no later than the end of 14 days after the date the Secretary of State serves on the special advocate the notice under rule 80.21(5)(b) or the material under rule 80.24(2), or such other period as the court may direct. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (4) Where the court fixes a hearing under this rule, the Secretary of State and the special advocate must before the hearing file with the court a schedule identifying the issues which cannot be agreed between them, which must also –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (a) give brief reasons for their contentions in relation to each issue; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (b) set out any proposals for the court to resolve those issues. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (5) A hearing under this rule shall take place in the absence of the relevant party and the relevant party’s legal representative. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (6) Where the court gives permission to the Secretary of State to withhold closed material, the court must –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (a) consider whether to direct the Secretary of State to serve a summary of that material on the relevant party and the relevant party’s legal representative; but

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (b) ensure that no such summary contains information or other material the disclosure of which would be contrary to the public interest. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (7) Where the court has not given permission to the Secretary of State to withhold closed material from, or has directed the Secretary of State to serve a summary of that material on, the relevant party and the relevant party’s legal representative –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (a) the Secretary of State shall not be required to serve that material or summary; but

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (b) if the Secretary of State does not do so, at a hearing on notice the court may –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (i) if it considers that the material or anything that is required to be summarised might be of assistance to the relevant party in relation to a matter under consideration by the court, direct that the matter is withdrawn from its consideration or that the Secretary of State makes such concessions or takes such other steps as the court specifies; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (ii) in any other case, direct that the Secretary of State shall not rely in the proceedings on that material or (as the case may be) on what is required to be summarised. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.25] (8) The court must give permission to the Secretary of State to withhold closed material where it considers that the disclosure of that material would be contrary to the public interest. ## Order of filing and serving material and written submissions

## 80.26

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.26] Subject to any directions given by the court, the parties must file and serve any material and written submissions, and the special advocate must file and serve any written submissions, in the following order –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.26] (a) the Secretary of State must file with the court any relevant material of which the Secretary of State is aware;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.26] (b) the Secretary of State must serve on –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.26] (i) the relevant party or the relevant party’s legal representative; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.26] (ii) the special advocate (as soon as one is appointed) or those instructing the special advocate,

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.26] any open material;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.26] (c) the relevant party must file with the court and serve on the Secretary of State and special advocate (if one is appointed) or those instructing the special advocate any written evidence which the relevant party wishes the court to take into account at the hearing;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.26] (d) the Secretary of State must file with the court any further relevant material;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.26] (e) the Secretary of State must serve on –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.26] (i) the relevant party or the relevant party’s legal representative; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.26] (ii) the special advocate (as soon as one is appointed) or those instructing the special advocate,

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.26] any open material filed with the court under paragraph (d);

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.26] (f) the Secretary of State must serve on the special advocate (if one has been appointed) any closed material;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.26] (g) the parties and the special advocate (if one has been appointed) must file and serve any written submissions as directed by the court. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.26] (Rules 80.24 and 80.25 will apply where any closed material is filed by the Secretary of State). ## Failure to comply with directions

## 80.27

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.27] (1) Where a party or the special advocate fails to comply with a direction of the court, the court may serve on that person a notice which states –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.27] (a) the respect in which that person has failed to comply with the direction;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.27] (b) a time limit for complying with the direction; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.27] (c) that the court may proceed to determine the proceedings before it, on the material available to it, if the party or special advocate fails to comply with the direction within the time specified. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.27] (2) Where a party or special advocate fails to comply with such a notice, the court may proceed in accordance with paragraph (1)(c). ## Judgments

## 80.28

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.28] (1) When the court gives judgment in any proceedings to which this Part applies, it may withhold any or part of its reasons if and to the extent that it is not possible to give those reasons without disclosing information contrary to the public interest. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.28] (2) Where the judgment of the court does not include the full reasons for its decision, the court must serve on the Secretary of State and the special advocate a separate written judgment including those reasons. ## Application by the Secretary of State for reconsideration of decision

## 80.29

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.29] (1) If the court proposes, in any proceedings to which this Part applies, to serve notice on a relevant party of any –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.29] (a) order or direction made or given in the absence of the Secretary of State; or

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.29] (b) any judgment,

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.29] then before the court serves any such notice on the relevant party, it must first serve notice on the Secretary of State of its intention to do so. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.29] (2) The Secretary of State may, within 5 days of being served with notice under paragraph (1), apply to the court to reconsider the terms of the order or direction or to review the terms of the proposed judgment if the Secretary of State considers that –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.29] (a) the Secretary of State’s compliance with the order or direction; or

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.29] (b) the notification to the relevant party of any matter contained in the judgment, order or direction;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.29] would cause information to be disclosed contrary to the public interest. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.29] (3) Where the Secretary of State makes an application under paragraph (2), the Secretary of State must at the same time serve on the special advocate, if one has been appointed –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.29] (a) a copy of the application; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.29] (b) a copy of the notice served on the Secretary of State pursuant to paragraph (1). [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.29] (4) Rule 80.25 (except for paragraphs (6) and (7)) shall, if a special advocate has been appointed, apply with any necessary modifications to the consideration of an application under paragraph (2) of this rule. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.29] (5) The court must not serve notice on the relevant party as mentioned in paragraph (1) before the time for the Secretary of State to make an application under paragraph (2) has expired. ## Supply of court documents

## 80.30

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.30] Unless the court otherwise directs, rule 5.4 (Register of Claims), rule 5.4B (Supply of documents from court records – a party) and rule 5.4C (Supply of court documents – a non-party) do not apply to any proceedings to which this Part applies.
